title: Linear Distinguishing Bound for XORed Random Permutations
summary: Earlier results are weaker or asymptotic; it remains to prove a query-linear, inverse-domain-size bound distinguishing two independent random permutations under XOR from a random function.

scope.domain: Finite-set probabilistic indistinguishability for the XOR of two independent random permutations versus a random function on the same set.
assumptions: The two random permutations are independent.
The adversary makes at most q queries.
parameters: C: an absolute positive constant independent of X, q, and A
X: the common domain and codomain of the permutations and random function
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish the conjectured advantage bound uniformly over X, q, and A.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The paper labels the bound Conjecture 1 against earlier weaker or asymptotic results. Its PWC, EPWC, and SCT security theorems assume the conjecture.
citation_labels: Thomas Peyrin et al., Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers
